newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - March 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - March 27.

text.p: The Washington Post carries the following stories on its front page on March 27:

WASHINGTON - Coalitions of civil rights groups and the mayor of New York yesterday filed separate suits to block a key provision of the nation's new welfare law, charging that it violates the constitutional rights of legal immigrants who will lose federal disability and food stamp benefits because they are not citizens.

RANCHO SANTA FE, CALIF - At least 49 bodies were discovered today inside a mansion of a multimillion-dollar estate, victims of what appeared to be a mass suicide, according to San Diego Sheriff spokesman Don Crist.

WASHINGTON - A new era is emerging on the nation's college campuses, one without campuses at all. Across academia, some students are starting to conduct their college careers almost entirely by personal computer.
BEIJING - Virce President Gore arrived in the Chinese capital this week as a man with two missions and two messages -- a task that at times proved to be too much.

CALI, COLOMBIA - Colombian drug traffickers, stung by the loss of markets and profits to rival Mexican organisations taking over the lucrative cocaine trade, are turning aggressively to heroin production and distribution, posing a major challenge to U.S. law enforcement officials.

WASHINGTON - A second suspect was arrested yesterday in connection with a string of home invasion robberies that have plagued Montgomery County neighborhoods for two months and police expressed confidence that the duo, knowne as the "Brit bandits" because they issued polite instructions in lilting English accents, are finished.
WASHINGTON - In a city government known for waste, mismanagement and inefficiency, Jay Carver's is an unusual story: He is a D.C. bureaucrat who has built a small agency into a national model.

WASHINGTON - Eldar Brizuels, a Peruvian housekeeper and former nanny, works 60 hours a week dusting furniture and vacuuming rugs for three Washington area families. Between jobs she rushes to ballet classes and soccer matches with her 8-year-old daughter. Her employers say she is terrific; her lifestyle is modest and she pays her income taxes faithfully.
